reality_delta: The implementation adds measurable criteria (text_hash, dom_summary_hash for browser; non-empty signups for signup; separate actionable_interactive_gate_marker from observed noise) as claimed. The two external tests confirm these work on round 20 data. However, 4 of 7 evidence items are self-referential (py_compile, design-check, self-check, redcap check) — they only prove internal consistency with the same codebase that defines the criteria. The changed_reality in the code is real; the changed_reality in behavior is plausible but 2 targeted tests on the same project that failed round 20 is insufficient to prove the fix generalizes. The interactive gate marker change — the most complex refactor — has zero dedicated test evidence beyond the diff itself.
main_concern: Verification is dominated by self-referential checks (4/7 items) that cannot detect false positives, edge cases, or generalization failures. The two external tests are both on round 20 data — the very project the implementation was designed to fix. Zero negative test cases exist. Zero generalization tests exist. The interactive gate marker refactor has no behavioral test evidence at all.
top_risks: Hash-based browser verification may false-positive on non-semantic DOM changes (timestamps, random IDs, animation states) that change text_hash but not actual UI state
Implementation validated only on round 20 project (the 'training set') — may fail on different project structures, interaction patterns, or signup formats in round 21
Interactive gate marker refactor untested — existing retry/failback flows that depend on old marker semantics could break silently in round 21 E2E
missing_evidence: Negative browser test cases: interactions that should correctly fail verification (e.g., clicking same element twice, clicking non-interactive elements)
Validation against at least one project other than round 20 to demonstrate the verifier generalizes beyond the failure case it was designed for
Controlled test of interactive gate marker retry/failback behavior: does marking observed noise separately from actionable markers preserve correct retry logic?
minimum_fix: Before round 21, run the verifier against at least one additional project not used in development. Add explicit negative browser test cases (same-element double-click should not pass, non-interactive element click should not pass). Verify interactive gate marker failback with a controlled retry scenario. Document the false-positive rate of hash-based detection against common DOM noise patterns (timestamps, random aria attributes, animation artifacts).
